title: Actuarial Practice Note: Measuring the Renewal Value of a SecureRate Contract, Deferred Fixed Annuities
content:
Practice note on the date and amount at which the renewal value of an Ashgrove SecureRate contract (Deferred Fixed Annuities) is measured for its default renewal.

## Rule

The renewal value is measured:

1. **Owner died before the renewal date** — on the date of death, as the contract value at the most recent interest credit grown at the expiring guaranteed rate for the actual calendar days from that credit to the date of death (a daily equivalent of the annual effective rate), rounded to the cent;
2. **Owner living, with an approved partial withdrawal request waiting to be paid** — as the renewal value less the amount that request asks for;
3. **Otherwise** — on the renewal date.

The renewal date is the day after the guarantee period end date, so an owner who died on or before the guarantee period end date died before the renewal date.

## Records read

- The owner's date of death, as recorded on the death claim on the contract.
- A partial withdrawal service request on the contract whose status is approved and which has not yet been paid, with the amount it asks for.

## Worked cases (hypothetical: contract value $120000.00 at the most recent interest credit on 10 January 2026, expiring rate 4.50%, renewal date 1 April 2026, renewal value $121177.92)

| Situation | Measured renewal value |
|---|---|
| Owner died on 1 March 2026 (50 days after the credit) | $120000.00 times 1.045 raised to the power of 50 over 365, that is $120725.75 |
| Owner living; an approved partial withdrawal request for $20000.00 is waiting | $121177.92 less $20000.00, that is $101177.92 |
| Owner living; no such request | $121177.92 |

Where the owner died before the renewal date, the date of death governs whether or not a withdrawal request is waiting.
